lesson_title: Run the Machine Backwards: Finding x When You Only Know y
hook_text: The rule is y equals 3x minus 2 and y is 10. Half the class puts the 10 in the wrong slot and gets 28. Here is the direction that matters.
clip_script: A rule like y equals 3x minus 2 is a machine: feed in x, out comes y. Feed in 1: 3 take away 2 is 1. Feed in 2: 4. Easy, that is forwards. Now the question says y is 10, find x. Ten came OUT. If you feed it IN you get 28, and that is the wrong direction. Run the machine backwards with undo buttons: the machine did times 3 then take away 2, so undo in reverse. Add 2 to 10: 12. Divide by 3: 4. In went 4. Check forwards: 3 times 4 is 12, take away 2 is 10. The pair is 4 semicolon 10, x first, y second, always. Squaring machines give two answers backwards: square then take away 1, out came 8, so in went 3 or negative 3. Read which number you were given, pick the direction, then go.
visual_style: A boxy machine on a whiteboard with an input slot and an output chute; a 10 bounces off the input slot in red, then slides into the output and travels backwards through lit-up undo buttons to become 4; the pair writes itself in brackets.
pacing: Forwards in two beats, the trap, the backwards run, the check, one twist.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson to build the tables that become next week's graphs.
